newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on crop weather, Refco sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on crop weather, Refco sales.

text.p: A more optimistic outlook for wheat crop production due to improved weather in France, Australia and the U.S. Great Plains plus aggressive selling by key fund trader Refco Inc drove CBOT soft red winter wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.
Lexington, Mass.-based Weather Services Corp forecast showers for the U.S. Plains overnight and the outlook was for additional rainfall in parts of the Plains states Saturday.
Also showers and cooler weather were seen returning to France Saturday and in Australia scattered rain had begun to fall in parts of the Australian state of Victoria.
Dry weather in some U.S. Plains areas, most of France and some key wheat areas of Australia had been leading to concerns about potential reductions in the wheat crops.
Refco Inc sold eight million bushels of July which helped trigger declines to the day's lows, traders said.

The recirculation of heavy deliveries posted this week on the May contract also weighed on prices. There were 2.820 million bushels of wheat posted Friday for delivery on the May contract amid weak stopping.
Wheat closed two to 8-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with May down 7-3/4 at $4.06-1/4. July was down 8-1/2 at $4.16-1/2.
